content:
Dear all:

I'm happy to share my recent work: Formalization of Harder-Narasimhan theory in Lean 4, with Mathlib ver 4.23.0.

Interestingly, high-level theories like the Harder-Narasimhan filtration can be formalized even if its algebraic geometric base hasn't been fully formalized yet. This is done by finding a suitable generalization of this theory in the context of order theory, which is general enough to cover the classical H-N theory and some useful generalizations in Arakelov geometry and other fields. (Why do I not choose to formalize the categorical version? Because this order theortic version is more feasible and is already general enough.) And once the algebraic geometry part of mathlib is solid, we can have the classical H-N filtration of vector bundles over curve with tiny effort.

Abstract:

The Harder-Narasimhan theory provides a canonical filtration of a vector bundle on a projective curve whose successive quotients are semistable with strictly decreasing slopes. In this article, we present the formalization of Harder-Narasimhan theory in the proof assistant Lean 4 with Mathlib. This formalization is based on a recent approach of Harder-Narasimhan theory by Chen and Jeannin, which reinterprets the theory in order-theoretic terms and avoids the classical dependence on algebraic geometry. As an application, we formalize the uniqueness of coprimary filtration of a finitely generated module over a noetherian ring, and the existence of the Jordan-Hölder filtration of a semistable Harder-Narasimhan game.

Paper link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19632
GitHub repo: https://github.com/YijunYuan/HarderNarasimhan

Remarks:

  1. There are two admitted lemmas related to associated primes. They are only used for the coprimiary filtration, which is an application of the main theory. These two lemmas are taken from reliable sources (Stacks Project and Bourbaki's Algèbre commutative). We hope they can be fully formalized in the future.
  2. Some code and coding style can be improved. I will maintain this project.
BTW, this project also serves as a full verification of Huayi Chen and Marion Jeannin's paper Harder-Narasimhan games
